posts.title: The one German sentence pattern that fails most Arabic speakers
posts.body:
If you are learning German for a call-center job, here is the single structure that trips up most Arabic speakers in the interview: the verb going to the end.

In Arabic and English you say "I want to help you today." In German, once you add a helper verb, the main verb jumps to the end: "Ich möchte Ihnen heute helfen." Helfen — help — lands last. Under pressure on a live call, people forget this and the sentence collapses.

The fix is not more grammar rules. It is saying the pattern out loud until your mouth does it without thinking. Take five sentences you would actually use with a customer, and drill them until the verb-final version feels normal.

That is exactly what the live interview trainer here is built to force — real pressure, real correction, in the structures a German employer will actually test. Practice it before the interview, not during it.
